metadata.title: Pecan Sticky Bread
metadata.description: Slow-rise maple pecan sticky buns with a buttery cinnamon caramel topping.
metadata.author: Sally McKenney
metadata.nutrition-note: Estimate based on ingredient totals; enriched dough with butter-heavy topping and filling

sections.title: Dough
steps: Whisk 1 cup whole milk(warmed to about 100°F/38°C), 2 tbsp granulated sugar, and 1.5 tbsp yeast in the bowl of a stand mixer fitted with a dough hook. Cover and let sit for 5 minutes until foamy on top.

On medium speed, beat in the remaining 0.5 cup granulated sugar and 0.5 cup unsalted butter(softened, cut into 4 pieces) until slightly broken up. Add 2 eggs(room temperature) and 0.5 tsp salt and beat until combined. Turn mixer to low and add 4.5 cups all-purpose flour 1 cup at a time, mixing fully before each addition. Beat 3 minutes until dough comes together and pulls away from the bowl sides.
Knead the dough in the mixer for an additional 5 minutes. Dough should be soft, smooth, and elastic. Poke it, if it slowly bounces back, it's ready.
Lightly grease a large bowl with 2 tsp oil. Place dough inside, turning to coat. Cover with a towel and allow to rise for 2 hours or until doubled in size.

sections.title: Topping
steps: Grease a #9x13 baking pan{}. Spread 2 cups chopped pecans in an even layer in the pan.

Combine 0.5 cup unsalted butter, 0.67 cup brown sugar, 0.25 cup whole milk, 0.25 cup pure maple syrup, and 0.25 tsp salt in a saucepan over medium heat. Stir until butter melts, then bring to a simmer. Simmer for 2 minutes, stirring occasionally. Remove from heat, whisk, then pour over the pecans. Set aside.

sections.title: Filling & Assembly
steps: Punch down the dough. On a lightly floured surface, roll into a 12×18-inch rectangle.
Spread 0.25 cup unsalted butter(softened) all over the dough. Mix 0.5 cup brown sugar and 2 tsp ground cinnamon in a small bowl, then sprinkle evenly over the butter.
Tightly roll up the dough into an 18-inch log. Cut into 12 even rolls and arrange in the prepared baking pan on top of the pecan topping.
Cover and let rise until puffy, about 35 minutes.
Preheat oven to 350°F (177°C). Bake for 26 minutes until golden-brown on top. Tent loosely with foil halfway through to prevent over-browning. Cool for 5 minutes.
Using oven mitts, carefully invert the pan onto a large serving platter. Serve warm.

sourceText:
== Dough ==

Whisk @whole milk{1%cup}(warmed to about 100°F/38°C), @granulated sugar{2%tbsp}, and @yeast{1.5%tbsp} in the bowl of a #stand mixer{} fitted with a #dough hook{}. Cover and let sit for ~{5%minutes} until foamy on top.

On medium speed, beat in the remaining @granulated sugar{0.5%cup} and @unsalted butter{0.5%cup}(softened, cut into 4 pieces) until slightly broken up. Add @eggs{2}(room temperature) and @salt{0.5%tsp} and beat until combined. Turn mixer to low and add @all-purpose flour{4.5%cups} 1 cup at a time, mixing fully before each addition. Beat ~{3%minutes} until dough comes together and pulls away from the bowl sides.

Knead the dough in the mixer for an additional ~{5%minutes}. Dough should be soft, smooth, and elastic. Poke it, if it slowly bounces back, it's ready.

Lightly grease a #large bowl{} with @oil{2%tsp}. Place dough inside, turning to coat. Cover with a towel and allow to rise for ~{2%hours} or until doubled in size.

== Topping ==

Grease a #9x13 baking pan{}. Spread @chopped pecans{2%cups} in an even layer in the pan.

Combine @unsalted butter{0.5%cup}, @brown sugar{0.67%cup}, @whole milk{0.25%cup}, @pure maple syrup{0.25%cup}, and @salt{0.25%tsp} in a #saucepan{} over medium heat. Stir until butter melts, then bring to a simmer. Simmer for ~{2%minutes}, stirring occasionally. Remove from heat, whisk, then pour over the pecans. Set aside.

== Filling & Assembly ==

Punch down the dough. On a lightly floured surface, roll into a 12×18-inch rectangle.

Spread @unsalted butter{0.25%cup}(softened) all over the dough. Mix @brown sugar{0.5%cup} and @ground cinnamon{2%tsp} in a small bowl, then sprinkle evenly over the butter.

Tightly roll up the dough into an 18-inch log. Cut into 12 even rolls and arrange in the prepared baking pan on top of the pecan topping.

Cover and let rise until puffy, about ~{35%minutes}.

Preheat oven to 350°F (177°C). Bake for ~{26%minutes} until golden-brown on top. Tent loosely with foil halfway through to prevent over-browning. Cool for ~{5%minutes}.

Using oven mitts, carefully invert the pan onto a large serving platter. Serve warm.

metadata.title: Perfectly Pillowy Cinnamon Rolls
metadata.description: Soft, pillowy cinnamon rolls with bold cinnamon flavor and rich vanilla icing. King Arthur's 2021 Recipe of the Year.

sections.title: Tangzhong
steps: Combine 1/2 cup milk and 3 tablespoons bread flour in a small saucepan and whisk until no lumps remain.
Place the saucepan over medium heat and cook the mixture, stirring regularly, until thickened, paste-like, and the spoon or spatula leaves lines on the bottom of the pan, 1-3 minutes.
Remove from the heat and transfer to a large mixing bowl or the bowl of a stand mixer.

sections.title: Dough
steps: Add 2/3 cup cold milk, 2 1/2 cups bread flour, 1 teaspoon table salt, 2 tablespoons granulated sugar, 2 teaspoons instant yeast, and 4 tablespoons unsalted butter (softened) to the mixing bowl with the tangzhong.
Mix to bring the dough together, then knead until smooth, elastic, and tacky, 10-15 minutes. If using a stand mixer with the dough hook on medium-low speed, 10-12 minutes.
Shape the dough into a ball, place it in a bowl, and cover with plastic wrap or a reusable cover.
Let the dough rise until puffy but not necessarily doubled in bulk, 60-90 minutes.

sections.title: Filling
steps: While the dough is rising, combine 1 tablespoon melted butter, 1/2 cup light brown sugar (packed), 2 tablespoons bread flour, 3 to 4 teaspoons cinnamon, and 1/16 teaspoon table salt in a medium bowl. Stir until the mixture is the texture of damp sand.
> Use the lesser amount of cinnamon for stronger varieties like Vietnamese (Saigon); the larger amount for milder cinnamons like Indonesian/Ceylon.
Lightly grease a baking sheet or line it with parchment paper.

sections.title: Assemble the Cinnamon Rolls
steps: Transfer the dough to a lightly greased work surface and press it into a 10" x 12" rectangle about 1/2" thick. For evenly shaped rolls, try to pat the dough into an actual rectangle with corners, rather than an oval.
Sprinkle the filling over the dough, covering all but a 1/2" strip along one long side.
Starting with the filling-covered long side, roll the dough into a log.

Score the dough lightly into eight equal 1 1/2" to 2" pieces, then cut at the score marks. Dental floss gives the cleanest cut: loop it underneath the log at the score mark and pull the ends in opposite directions to cut.
Place the cinnamon rolls onto the prepared baking sheet, spacing them at least 2" apart in a 3-2-3 arrangement. Tuck the ends of the spirals underneath so they stay in place.
Cover with lightly greased plastic wrap or a reusable cover and let rise, 30-60 minutes, until puffy and the dough doesn't bounce back immediately when gently pressed.

sections.title: Bake
steps: About 20 minutes before baking, position a rack in the top third of the oven and preheat the oven to 375°F.

Bake the cinnamon rolls for 14-18 minutes, until light golden brown and a digital thermometer inserted into the center reads 190°F. Bake for the shorter time for extra-soft rolls, the longer time for more color and slightly firmer texture.
Remove from the oven, place the pan on a rack, and brush the hot rolls with 1 1/2 tablespoons melted butter.
Let the cinnamon rolls cool, 10-15 minutes, before icing.

sections.title: Icing
steps: Combine the remaining 1 1/2 tablespoons melted butter with 1/2 teaspoon vanilla extract, 1/16 teaspoon table salt, confectioners' sugar{1 1/2%cups} (sifted), and 1 to 2 tablespoons milk (enough to thin to desired consistency) in a medium bowl. Mix with a spatula until smooth.
> Milk makes a lovely frosting; cream adds richness, buttermilk adds subtle tang.
Ice the cinnamon rolls and serve immediately. If serving later, wait to ice until just before serving.

sections.title: Storage
steps: Store completely cooled cinnamon rolls, un-iced and well wrapped, for a couple of days at room temperature or freeze for up to 1 month.

> For overnight cinnamon rolls: bake the day before, store tightly sealed and un-iced at room temperature overnight. The next morning, cover with foil and warm in a 300°F to 350°F oven for 5 to 10 minutes. Spread with icing and enjoy.
> For cream cheese frosting: stir in 4 to 6 tablespoons softened cream cheese to the icing along with the other ingredients.

sourceText:
== Tangzhong ==

Combine @milk{1/2%cup} and @bread flour{3%tablespoons} in a small #saucepan{} and whisk until no lumps remain.

Place the #saucepan{} over medium heat and cook the mixture, stirring regularly, until thickened, paste-like, and the spoon or spatula leaves lines on the bottom of the pan, ~{1-3%minutes}.

Remove from the heat and transfer to a large #mixing bowl{} or the bowl of a #stand mixer{}.

== Dough ==

Add @cold milk{2/3%cup}, @bread flour{2 1/2%cups}, @table salt{1%teaspoon}, @granulated sugar{2%tablespoons}, @instant yeast{2%teaspoons}, and @unsalted butter{4%tablespoons} (softened) to the mixing bowl with the tangzhong.

Mix to bring the dough together, then knead until smooth, elastic, and tacky, ~{10-15%minutes}. If using a #stand mixer{} with the dough hook on medium-low speed, ~{10-12%minutes}.

Shape the dough into a ball, place it in a #bowl{}, and cover with plastic wrap or a reusable cover.

Let the dough rise until puffy but not necessarily doubled in bulk, ~{60-90%minutes}.

== Filling ==

While the dough is rising, combine @melted butter{1%tablespoon}, @light brown sugar{1/2%cup} (packed), @bread flour{2%tablespoons}, @cinnamon{3 to 4%teaspoons}, and @table salt{1/16%teaspoon} in a medium #bowl{}. Stir until the mixture is the texture of damp sand.

> Use the lesser amount of cinnamon for stronger varieties like Vietnamese (Saigon); the larger amount for milder cinnamons like Indonesian/Ceylon.

Lightly grease a #baking sheet{} or line it with parchment paper.

== Assemble the Cinnamon Rolls ==

Transfer the dough to a lightly greased work surface and press it into a 10" x 12" rectangle about 1/2" thick. For evenly shaped rolls, try to pat the dough into an actual rectangle with corners, rather than an oval.

Sprinkle the filling over the dough, covering all but a 1/2" strip along one long side.

Starting with the filling-covered long side, roll the dough into a log.

Score the dough lightly into eight equal 1 1/2" to 2" pieces, then cut at the score marks. Dental floss gives the cleanest cut: loop it underneath the log at the score mark and pull the ends in opposite directions to cut.

Place the cinnamon rolls onto the prepared #baking sheet{}, spacing them at least 2" apart in a 3-2-3 arrangement. Tuck the ends of the spirals underneath so they stay in place.

Cover with lightly greased plastic wrap or a reusable cover and let rise, ~{30-60%minutes}, until puffy and the dough doesn't bounce back immediately when gently pressed.

== Bake ==

About ~{20%minutes} before baking, position a rack in the top third of the oven and preheat the oven to 375°F.

Bake the cinnamon rolls for ~{14-18%minutes}, until light golden brown and a digital thermometer inserted into the center reads 190°F. Bake for the shorter time for extra-soft rolls, the longer time for more color and slightly firmer texture.

Remove from the oven, place the pan on a #rack{}, and brush the hot rolls with @melted butter{1 1/2%tablespoons}.

Let the cinnamon rolls cool, ~{10-15%minutes}, before icing.

== Icing ==

Combine the remaining @melted butter{1 1/2%tablespoons} with @vanilla extract{1/2%teaspoon}, @table salt{1/16%teaspoon}, @confectioners{}' sugar{1 1/2%cups} (sifted), and @milk{1 to 2%tablespoons} (enough to thin to desired consistency) in a medium #bowl{}. Mix with a #spatula{} until smooth.

> Milk makes a lovely frosting; cream adds richness, buttermilk adds subtle tang.

Ice the cinnamon rolls and serve immediately. If serving later, wait to ice until just before serving.

== Storage ==

Store completely cooled cinnamon rolls, un-iced and well wrapped, for a couple of days at room temperature or freeze for up to 1 month.

> For overnight cinnamon rolls: bake the day before, store tightly sealed and un-iced at room temperature overnight. The next morning, cover with foil and warm in a 300°F to 350°F oven for 5 to 10 minutes. Spread with icing and enjoy.

> For cream cheese frosting: stir in 4 to 6 tablespoons softened cream cheese to the icing along with the other ingredients.

metadata.title: Pesto

metadata.title: Philly Roll with Dough Conditioner
metadata.description: Bread rolls for Philly cheese steak sandwiches, made with commercial dough conditioner for improved texture and moisture.

sections.title: Yeast Starter
steps: In a small bowl, combine 120 g lukewarm water, 5 g sugar, and 8 g active dry yeast. Let stand 10-15 minutes until foamy.

sections.title: Dough
steps: In the bowl of a stand mixer fitted with a dough hook, combine 540 g bread flour, 10 g sugar, 12 g salt, and 9 g dough conditioner.
Add the yeast mixture and 240 g lukewarm water to the flour mixture. Mix on low speed for 5 minutes until the dough starts to come together.
Add 30 g olive oil and continue kneading for 5 minutes until the dough is smooth and elastic.

sections.title: Hand Kneading
steps: Turn the dough out onto a very lightly floured work surface and knead by hand for 5 minutes, using as little extra flour as possible.

sections.title: First Rise
steps: Place the dough in a lightly oiled bowl, cover with plastic wrap, and let rise in a warm place for 1 hour or until doubled in size.

sections.title: Shaping
steps: Gently deflate the dough and divide into 6-8 equal portions (90-67g each). Shape each portion into rolls about 15-18cm long.
Place the shaped rolls on a parchment-lined baking sheet, cover loosely with plastic wrap, and let rise for 45-60 minutes until nearly doubled in size.

sections.title: Oven Baking
steps: Preheat your oven to 425 F. Place a small tray of boiling water in the back corner of the oven to create humidity.
Using a sharp knife or razor blade, cut a shallow slit down the center of each roll.
Bake for 10 minutes, then reduce the heat to 400 F and bake for an additional 20-25 minutes until the rolls are an even golden brown and sound hollow when tapped.
> The dough conditioner helps maintain moisture inside the roll even during longer bakes.

sections.title: Bread Cloche Variation
steps: Preheat your bread cloche in the oven at 475 F for at least 30 minutes.
Place 2-3 shaped rolls on parchment paper, loosely cover, and let rise for the final time (45 minutes).
Carefully remove the hot cloche from the oven, remove the lid, and transfer the risen dough on the parchment paper into the cloche.
Using a sharp knife or razor blade, cut a shallow slit down the center of each roll.
Cover with the cloche lid and return to the oven. Bake covered for 15 minutes. Remove the lid and bake for an additional 10-15 minutes until golden brown and hollow when tapped.

sections.title: Cooling
steps: Transfer the rolls to a wire rack to cool before using for your Philly cheese steak sandwiches.

metadata.title: Philly Sandwich Rolls
metadata.description: Philadelphia-style sandwich rolls with same-day and overnight fermentation methods. A bread cloche creates the perfect environment for a thin, crispy crust and light, airy interior.

sections.title: Equipment
steps: bread cloche or Dutch oven
digital scale
stand mixer or mixing bowl
dough scraper
baking parchment
spray bottle

sections.title: Same-Day Method
steps: Combine 500 g bread flour and 10 g diastatic malt powder in the stand mixer bowl.
Mix 320 g water at 70F/21C with 5 g instant yeast in a separate container. Add the wet ingredients to the dry and mix until just combined. Cover and autolyse for 20 minutes.
Add 9 g salt and 15 g neutral oil. Mix on medium-low speed until the dough is smooth and passes the window pane test. Dough temperature should be 75-78F (24-26C).
Transfer to a lightly oiled container. Perform 3 sets of stretch and folds at 30 minute intervals. Let rise until doubled, about 2 hours.
Divide into 8 equal portions, about 140g each. Shape into balls and rest 15 minutes covered.

Shape each ball into a 6-7 inch oval. Place on baking parchment, cover with a damp cloth, and proof until puffy, about 45-60 minutes. Brush with water and add to taste sesame seeds if using. Score lengthwise.
Preheat oven and bread cloche or Dutch oven to 450F (230C) for 45 minutes.
Bake 2-3 rolls at a time: covered for the first 10 minutes, then uncovered until golden brown, 10-15 minutes more.
Cool on a wire rack a minimum of 30 minutes before cutting.
> Spritz rolls with water just before closing the cloche for better steam.

sections.title: Evening Mix (Day 1)
steps: Follow the same mixing process as above with these modifications: use cold water (45F/7C) and reduce yeast to 2 g instant yeast.
After initial bulk fermentation of about 1 hour with 2 sets of folds, transfer to the refrigerator and store overnight for 12-15 hours.

sections.title: Morning Process (Day 2)
steps: Remove dough from the refrigerator and rest at room temperature for 1 hour.
Proceed with dividing and shaping as above. Final proof will take longer, about 60-90 minutes.
Bake following the same cloche method.
> Maintain dough temperature. Use cold water if the kitchen is warm.
> Rolls should feel light and puffy before baking.
> Ensure the cloche is thoroughly preheated for 45+ minutes.
> Do not rush the cooling process, it affects final texture.
> If crust is too thick, reduce uncovered baking time.
> If interior is dense, extend final proofing time.
> If holes are too large, reduce bulk fermentation time.
> If crust is too pale, increase uncovered baking time.

sections.title: Storage
steps: Best used same day. Store in a paper bag up to 2 days. Freeze up to 3 months. Refresh in a 350F oven for 5 minutes before using.
> Recipe can be doubled but maintain the same baking batch size of 2-3 rolls per cloche.

metadata.title: Pico de Gallo
metadata.description: Fresh tomato salsa with onion, chiles, cilantro, and lime juice.

sections.title: Drain Tomatoes
steps: Season 1.5 lb ripe tomatoes (cut into 1/4- to 1/2-inch dice, about 3 cups) with 1 tsp kosher salt and toss to combine. Transfer to a fine-mesh strainer set in a bowl and allow to drain for 20-30 minutes. Discard liquid.

sections.title: Combine
steps: Combine drained tomatoes with 0.5 white onion (finely diced, about 3/4 cup), 1-2 serrano or jalapeno chiles (finely diced, seeds and membranes removed for milder salsa), 0.5 cup fresh cilantro (finely chopped leaves), and 1 tbsp lime juice (from 1 lime). Toss to combine and season to taste with salt.
> Use the ripest tomatoes you can find. In the off-season, smaller plum, Roma, or cherry tomatoes work best.
> Pico de gallo keeps for up to 3 days in the refrigerator in a tightly sealed container.

metadata.title: Pizza Buns
metadata.description: Savory buns with pizza filling, perfect for parties, picnics, or snacking on the go.

cookware: baking sheets lined with parchment or lightly greased

sections.title: Dough
steps: Place 1 1/4 cups milk, 3 tbsp olive oil, 1 1/2 tsp salt, 3 1/2 cups bread flour, and 2 1/2 tsp instant yeast into a bowl. Mix and knead by hand, using a stand mixer, or in a bread machine to make a smooth, soft dough.
Place the dough in a lightly greased bowl, cover, and allow to rise until doubled, 60-90 minutes.

sections.title: Assembly
steps: Gently deflate the dough and transfer to a lightly greased work surface. Roll the dough into a 12" x 18" rectangle.
Spread evenly with 1/2 cup pizza sauce, 2 cups shredded mozzarella cheese, and 1 cup pepperoni chopped.
> Feel free to replace the pepperoni with about 1 cup of your favorite cooked pizza toppings. Chop chunky toppings like sliced mushrooms or peppers rather than leaving them whole.
Starting with a long end, roll the dough into a log. Cut the log into 12 to 18 pieces depending on how large you want the buns.
Space the rounds on two baking sheets lined with parchment or lightly greased. If you've cut 12 rounds, flatten them gently to about 1" tall.
Cover the pans and allow the buns to rise 60-90 minutes until nicely puffed. Towards the end of the rising time, preheat the oven to 350°F.

sections.title: Bake
steps: Bake the buns for 25-30 minutes until light golden brown.
Remove from the oven and serve warm with additional pizza sauce on the side if desired.
> Store leftovers in the refrigerator. Reheat for about 10 minutes, covered, in a 350°F oven or briefly in the microwave.

metadata.title: Pizza Crust
metadata.description: Classic homemade pizza crust, makes 1 or 2 standard round pizzas or 1 large rectangular pizza.

sections.title: Activate Yeast
steps: If using 2 tsp active dry yeast, dissolve with a pinch of 1 pinch sugar in 2 tbsp lukewarm water. Let sit for 15 minutes until bubbly.
> Skip this step for 2 tsp instant yeast.

sections.title: Combine Ingredients
steps: Weigh or spoon and level the 3 cups all-purpose flour. Mix and knead together with 7/8 cup lukewarm water, 2 tbsp olive oil, and 1.25 tsp table salt by hand, mixer, or bread machine until you have a soft, smooth dough.
If kneading in a stand mixer, it should take 4-5 minutes at medium speed. The dough should clean the sides of the bowl but may stick a bit at the bottom.

sections.title: Make Pizza Now
steps: Place the dough in a greased bowl, cover, and let it rise until puffy, 1 hour for instant yeast, 90 minutes for active dry yeast.

sections.title: Make Pizza Later
steps: Let the dough rise for 45 minutes at room temperature, then refrigerate for 4-24 hours. Remove from the fridge 2-3 hours before baking.

sections.title: Shape and Prepare
steps: Decide your pizza size and shape. Divide the dough in half for two pizzas or keep it whole for one. Let the dough rest, covered, for 15 minutes before shaping it in the pan.

sections.title: Bake the Crust
steps: Preheat the oven to 450F. Bake the untopped pizza on the lower rack until set and slightly browned around the edges, 8-14 minutes depending on thickness.

sections.title: Add Toppings
steps: Remove from the oven, add toppings, and return to the upper rack. Bake for another 10-15 minutes until the crust is browned and the cheese is melted.

sections.title: Serve
steps: Cool slightly on a rack before serving. For easiest slicing, use scissors.
> Refrigerate dough overnight for better flavor.
> Use a baking stone for a crispier crust.
> Freeze partially baked crusts for up to 3 months.

metadata.title: Pizza Sauce
metadata.description: A blend of New York and Neapolitan styles for a sauce that's fresh, flavorful, and versatile for various pizza styles.

sections.title: Get Started
steps: Open the 1 28-ounce can San Marzano whole peeled tomatoes (DOP certified preferred). Gently crush each tomato with your hands, removing any tough cores or stems. This can also be done in a bowl.
> Using high-quality San Marzano tomatoes makes a huge difference in the flavor of the sauce. If you can't find them, use another good quality canned tomato.

sections.title: Saute Aromatics
steps: In a large skillet or saucepan, heat the 1/4 cup extra virgin olive oil over medium heat.
Add the 2 cloves garlic (minced) and cook for 1 minute, until fragrant but not browned. Be careful not to burn the garlic.

sections.title: Simmer the Sauce
steps: Add the crushed tomatoes to the skillet.
Stir in the 1 tsp dried oregano, 1/2 tsp dried basil, 1/4 tsp red pepper flakes (optional), 1/2 tsp sugar (or 1 tsp balsamic vinegar), and 1/2 tsp kosher salt (or to taste).
Bring the sauce to a gentle simmer, then reduce the heat to low and cover. Simmer for 15-20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the sauce has thickened slightly and the flavors have melded.

sections.title: Adjust Texture

In a #large skillet or saucepan{}, heat the @extra virgin olive oil{1/4%cup} over medium heat.

Stir in the @dried oregano{1%tsp}, @dried basil{1/2%tsp}, @red pepper flakes{1/4%tsp} (optional), @sugar{1/2%tsp} (or @balsamic vinegar{1%tsp}), and @kosher salt{1/2%tsp} (or to taste).

> Adjust the texture to your preference. Some people like a smooth sauce, while others prefer it chunky.

metadata.title: Pork And Chive Dumplings
metadata.description: Juicy Chinese pork dumplings with garlic chives, infused Sichuan peppercorn oil, and a ginger-scallion puree for extra moisture.
metadata.nutrition-note: Nutrition from source, total for 8 servings. Makes about 4 dozen dumplings.

sections.title: Infused Oil
steps: To a small saucepan over medium heat, add 0.25 cup neutral oil, 1 tbsp Sichuan peppercorns, 1 star anise, and 5 cloves garlic. Heat for 5 minutes infuse until the garlic is lightly browned. Remove from heat and let cool.

sections.title: Ginger Scallion Puree
steps: Add 0.75 cup water, 1 tbsp fresh ginger, chopped, and 0.33 cup scallion, roughly chopped, to a food processor. Puree until smooth.

sections.title: Filling
steps: Add 1 lb ground pork to a mixing bowl. Add the ginger scallion puree in three batches, whipping in one direction until the pork completely absorbs the liquid before adding the next batch.

Add 1 tbsp oyster sauce, 1 tbsp light soy sauce, 2 tsp dark soy sauce, 1.5 tsp sesame oil, 1 tsp sugar, 0.5 tsp white pepper, 0.5 tsp five spice powder, and 0.5 tsp salt. Mix well, whipping in one direction until the mixture resembles a paste.
In a separate bowl, mix together 2 cups Chinese garlic chives, finely chopped, and the infused oil poured through a strainer. Combine the chives with the meat mixture and whip until well-combined.
> The chives must be finely chopped or the filling may not bind together as well.

sections.title: Assembly
steps: Set up a sheet pan lined with parchment paper, a small bowl of water, and keep 2 packs dumpling wrappers under a damp paper towel to prevent drying.

To assemble, dip your finger in water and wet the outer edges of a round wrapper. Add about 1 tablespoon of filling to the center and pleat closed, making sure the dumpling is tightly sealed. Place on the parchment-lined sheet pan spaced slightly apart. Repeat until you've run out of filling or wrappers.
> Steam, pan-fry, or boil following your preferred dumpling cooking method.
> To freeze, cover the tray with plastic bags and place in the freezer overnight. Once frozen solid, transfer to freezer bags for up to 2 months.

metadata.title: Potatoes with Sesame Seeds
metadata.description: Easy, delicious Til Ke Aloo, waxy potatoes stir-fried with cumin, mustard, and sesame seeds. Pairs well with Indian meals or simple roasted and grilled meats.

steps: Boil the 1 kg waxy potatoes in their jackets. Drain and cool them for 3-4 hours. Peel the potatoes and chop them into 2cm cubes.

sections.title: Cook
steps: Heat the 6 tbsp vegetable oil in a 25-30cm frying-pan over a medium flame. When the oil is very hot, put in the 2 tsp cumin seeds, 2 tsp black mustard seeds and 2 tbsp sesame seeds. As soon as the seeds begin to pop, put in the chopped potatoes. Stir and fry the potatoes for about 5 minutes.
> A non-stick or well-seasoned cast-iron frying pan works best.
> Look for a few brown spots on the potatoes for best flavor.

sections.title: Season
steps: Add the 2 tsp salt, 0.5 tsp Kashmiri chilli powder and 1 tbsp lemon juice. Stir and fry for another 3 minutes.

metadata.title: Pumpkin Bread
metadata.description: Super-moist pumpkin bread packed with flavor. Can be made as a simple loaf or enhanced with chocolate chips and/or nuts.

sections.title: Bread
steps: In a large bowl, beat together 1 cup vegetable oil, 2 2/3 cups granulated sugar, 4 large eggs, 2 cups pumpkin puree, and 2/3 cup water.
Add 3 1/3 cups all-purpose flour, 1/2 tsp baking powder, 1 tsp baking soda, 1 1/2 tsp table salt, 1 tsp nutmeg, and 1 tsp vanilla extract, stirring to combine.

Mix in 1 1/2 cups chocolate chips and 1 cup chopped walnuts or pecans, if using. To make one loaf with chips/nuts and one without, divide the batter in half. Leave one half plain, and add 3/4 cup chips and 1/2 cup nuts to the other half.
Preheat the oven to 350F. Lightly grease two 8 1/2" x 4 1/2" loaf pans for the plain version, two 9" x 5" loaf pans if adding chocolate chips and nuts, or one of each.
Spoon the batter into the prepared pans. Sprinkle the tops with to taste coarse sparkling sugar.
Bake the bread for 60 minutes to 80 minutes, or until a cake tester or toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean.
Remove the bread from the oven and cool on a cooling rack. When completely cool, wrap well in plastic and store overnight before serving.
> Waiting to enjoy the bread allows the flavors to meld and texture to completely set.

sections.title: Glaze (optional)
steps: Stir together 1 cup confectioners sugar and 2 tbsp butter (melted), then add 1 tbsp milk. Drizzle the glaze over the bread and cut into slices to serve.
> Substitute diced crystallized ginger, golden raisins, or dried cranberries for the chocolate chips and/or nuts.
> This recipe makes eight 3" x 5" gift loaves with the addition of chips and nuts. Bake 45 to 60 minutes, start testing at 45 minutes.
> Store leftover bread, tightly wrapped, at room temperature for several days. Freeze for longer storage.

metadata.title: Quick Pickled Vegetables
metadata.description: I like quick pickled vegetables just as much as naturally fermented. This recipe is easy, works with many vegetables, and keeps for months.

steps: Fill a large jar with the desired vegetables and any fresh herbs and garlic (for example, cucumbers and sprigs of sage), leaving a bit of headspace.

In a medium pot, combine the 350 ml vinegar, 250 ml water, and 8 g salt. Add the desired aromatics (for example, Sichuan peppercorns, toasted coriander seeds, and mustard seeds), excluding fresh herbs and garlic. Bring the mixture to a boil. As soon as the liquid comes to a boil and the salt is fully dissolved, turn off the heat.

Pour the hot pickling liquid with the aromatics directly over the vegetables until they are fully submerged. To keep the vegetables from floating, place a paper towel folded to fit in the top of the jar over the vegetables. Keep the jar uncovered, and let it cool to room temperature.

Once the liquid has cooled completely, remove the paper towel and screw the lid onto the jar. Refrigerate. Your pickles are done and ready to be enjoyed at any time. These will last for several months in the refrigerator.

metadata.title: Quick-Pickled Onions
metadata.description: Tangy and crisp pickled onions ready in 30 minutes. The perfect condiment for tacos, burritos, nachos, burgers and more.

steps: Pack the 1 medium red onion into a 1-pint mason jar or similar heat-safe vessel. Place the jar in the sink, to catch any splashes of hot vinegar later.

In a small saucepan, combine the 0.5 cup water, both vinegars, 1.5 tbsp maple syrup, 1.5 tsp fine sea salt, and 0.25 tsp red pepper flakes. Bring the mixture to a gentle simmer over medium heat, then carefully pour the mixture into the jar over the onions.

Use a butter knife or spoon to press the onions down into the vinegar and pop any air bubbles in the jar. Let the pickled onions cool to room temperature, 20 minutes to 30 minutes, at which point they should be sufficiently pickled for serving.
Cover and refrigerate leftover pickled onions for later.
> Quick-pickled onions are best consumed within three days, but they keep for 2 to 3 weeks in the refrigerator.

metadata.title: Ratatouille
metadata.description: A tasty fall vegetarian dish with sliced eggplan, squash, zuchini, and tomatoes

steps: Preheat the oven for 375˚F (190˚C).
Slice the 2 eggplant, tomatoes,{6} 2 squash, and 2 zucchini into approximately ¹⁄₁₆-inch (1-mm) rounds, then set aside.
For the sauce: Heat the 2 tbsp olive oil in a #12-inch (30-cm) oven-safe pan{} over medium-high heat.
Sauté the 1 diced onion, 4 cloves minced garlic, 2 diced  bell pepper, until soft, about 10 minutes. Season with salt and pepper, then add the 28 oz crushed tomatoes.
Stir until the ingredients are fully incorporated. Remove from heat, then add the 10 leaves basil. Stir once more, then smooth the surface of the sauce with a spatula.
Arrange the sliced veggies in alternating patterns, (for example, eggplant, tomato, squash, zucchini) on top of the sauce from the outer edge to the middle of the pan. Season with salt and pepper.

For the herb seasoning: In a small bowl, mix together the 10 leaves basil, 1 tsp minced garlic, 2 tbsp parsley, 2 tsp thyme, salt, pepper, and 4 tbsp olive oil. Spoon the herb seasoning over the vegetables.
Cover the pan with foil and bake for 40 minutes. Uncover, then bake for another 20 minutes, until the vegetables are softened.
Serve while hot as a main dish or side.
The ratatouille is also excellent the next day cover with foil and reheat in a 350˚F (180˚C) oven for 15 minutes, or simply microwave to desired temperature.

metadata.title: Red Lentils with Cumin Seeds
metadata.description: Masoor dal, salmon-coloured split peas that turn dull yellow when cooked, tempered with cumin seeds and spices. Best served with rice and almost any Indian meat or vegetable dish.

sections.title: Cook the Lentils
steps: Combine the 200 gram red split lentils (masoor dal), picked over, washed and drained, and 1 litre water in a heavy pot. Bring to a simmer. Remove any scum that collects at the top. Add the 2 thin slices fresh ginger (unpeeled) and 0.5 tsp ground turmeric. Stir to mix. Cover, leaving the lid very slightly ajar, reduce the heat to low and simmer gently for 45-60 minutes or until the lentils are tender. Stir every 5 minutes during the last half hour to prevent sticking. Add the 1 tsp salt (or to taste) and stir to mix. Remove the ginger slices.

sections.title: Temper the Spices
steps: Heat the 3 tbsp ghee (or vegetable oil) in a small frying pan over a medium flame. When hot, put in a pinch of ground asafoetida. A second later, put in the 1 tsp cumin seeds. Let the seeds sizzle for a few seconds. Now put in the 1 tsp ground coriander seeds and 0.25 tsp cayenne pepper. Stir once and then quickly pour the contents of the pan, ghee and spices, into the pot with the lentils. Stir to mix.

sections.title: Serve
steps: Sprinkle the 2 tbsp fresh green coriander (finely chopped) over the top when you serve.

metadata.title: Roast Broccolini
metadata.description: Oven-roasted broccolini with garlic, an easy, nutritious 25-minute side dish.

steps: Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C).
Trim the woody ends from 2 bunches broccolini (baby broccoli, just shy of 1 pound) and arrange on a sheet pan.

Drizzle with 2.5 tbsp extra virgin olive oil (do not skimp or it may burn) and scatter over smashed and peeled 3 cloves garlic. Season with 0.5 tsp kosher salt and 0.25 tsp black pepper, then toss to coat evenly.
Roast for 15 minutes, until the stems are tender-crisp and the tips are deeply browned.
Serve hot with an extra pinch of salt.

metadata.title: Saag Aloo
metadata.description: Indian spinach and potato curry, served with Rogan josh and Indian bread or rice.

sections.title: Cook the Spinach
steps: Bring the 275 ml water to the boil in a saucepan. Put in the 550 g frozen leaf spinach, cover and cook until just done. Drain in a colander and rinse under cold running water. Press out most of the liquid in the leaves and then chop them coarsely.

sections.title: Prepare the Aromatics
steps: Cut the 110 g onions in half lengthways, then across into very fine slices.

sections.title: Fry and Simmer
steps: Heat the 5 tbsp vegetable oil in a heavy saucepan over a medium flame. When hot, put in the 1 pinch ground asafoetida and then, a second later, the 2 tsp black mustard seeds. As soon as the mustard seeds begin to pop, put in the 110 g onions and 2 garlic cloves, peeled and finely chopped. Stir and fry for 2 minutes.
> Asafoetida is optional but adds authentic flavor.
Put in the 500 g waxy potatoes, peeled and cut roughly into 2-2.5cm cubes, and 0.25-0.5 tsp cayenne pepper. Stir and fry for 1 minute.
> Waxy potatoes hold their shape better than floury varieties.

Now put in the spinach, 1 tsp salt and 2 tbsp water. Bring to the boil. Cover tightly, reduce the heat to very low and cook gently for 40 minutes or until the potatoes are tender. Stir a few times during the cooking period and make sure that there is always a little liquid in the pot.

metadata.title: Sandwich Rye Bread
metadata.description: Easy-to-slice rye bread with dill pickle juice for tang and moist texture. Perfect for pastrami, corned beef, a Reuben, or grilled Swiss sandwiches.

sections.title: Dough
steps: Combine 2.5 tsp instant yeast or 2.5 tsp active dry yeast, 2/3 to 7/8 cup water lukewarm, 1/4 cup vegetable oil, 3/4 cup dill pickle juice, 1.5 tsp table salt, 1 tbsp granulated sugar, 1.25 tsp caraway seeds, 1.25 tsp dill seeds, 1 tbsp mustard seeds or Dijon mustard, 3/4 cup dried potato flakes or potato flour, 2.5 cups bread flour, and 1 1/3 cups rye flour or pumpernickel flour.
Mix until clumps form. Let the dough rest 20 minutes for the flour to start absorbing the liquid.

Knead the dough by stand mixer with dough hook at second speed for about 7 minutes to make a stiff but fairly smooth dough. The dough should clean the sides of the bowl; if it doesn't, sprinkle in a bit more all-purpose flour.
> We don't recommend kneading this dough by hand, as it's hard to develop the gluten sufficiently. If you do knead by hand, the dough will take longer to rise and won't rise as high.

sections.title: First Rise
steps: Place the dough in a lightly greased bowl, cover, and let rise until puffy, 1-2 hours. It may or may not have doubled in bulk, but it will have expanded.

sections.title: Shaping
steps: Gently deflate the dough and shape it into a log. Place the log in a lightly greased loaf pan (8.5" x 4.5" for stiffer dough, or 9" x 5" for slacker dough). Press it to the edges of the pan and flatten the top.

sections.title: Second Rise
steps: Tent the pan with greased plastic wrap and allow the loaf to rise until crowned about 1" to 1.5" over the edge of the pan, 1-1.5 hours. Towards the end of the rising time, preheat the oven to 350F.

sections.title: Baking
steps: Bake the bread for 20 minutes. Tent it lightly with foil and bake for an additional 20 minutes. When done the bread will be golden brown and its internal temperature will register 190F on an instant-read thermometer.
Remove the bread from the oven, wait 5 minutes, then remove it from the pan and allow it to cool completely on a rack before slicing. Store for up to a week at cool room temperature.

> This bread has a sensitive liquid-flour ratio. The finished dough should be smooth and easy to handle; it shouldn't be sticky. If it's sticky, the rising times may be shorter; a slacker dough usually rises faster than one that's stiffer.
> Use the lesser amount of water in summer or a humid environment, the greater amount in winter or a dry climate, and somewhere in between the rest of the year.

> For a wonderfully close-grained, square-corner sandwich loaf, press the dough into a 9" x 4" pain de mie pan. Bake as directed, removing the cover and tenting loosely with foil for the final 15 minutes of baking.
> This is a great place to use discard sourdough starter. Substitute up to 1 cup starter for an equal weight of bread flour and water.

metadata.title: Scallion Dipping Sauce
metadata.description: Salty, spicy, and tangy, this soy-based seasoning is an easy way to boost the flavor of whatever you're eating, which is why you should always have a container on hand (plus, it'll keep in the refrigerator for ages). Try it over anything crispy or starchy,think dumplings, pancakes, fried chicken, fried rice, or potatoes,or drizzle it into soup broths or a bowl of noodles.

steps: Combine 28 g toasted sesame seeds, 480 ml soy sauce, 42 g chili flakes, 120 ml toasted sesame oil, 180 ml rice vinegar, 28 g sugar, and 1 bunch scallions (about 8 scallions), trimmed and thinly sliced.
Whisk or stir them until they're well mixed.
Adjust the seasoning to taste, and add a little water if you want the sauce to be mellower in flavor.
Pour the sauce into a sealable jar or container, and store it in the refrigerator for up to 3 months.

sourceText:
Combine @toasted sesame seeds{28%g}, @soy sauce{480%ml}, @chili flakes{42%g}, @toasted sesame oil{120%ml}, @rice vinegar{180%ml}, @sugar{28%g}, and @scallions{1%bunch} (about 8 scallions), trimmed and thinly sliced.

Whisk or stir them until they're well mixed.

Adjust the seasoning to taste, and add a little water if you want the sauce to be mellower in flavor.

Pour the sauce into a sealable jar or container, and store it in the refrigerator for up to 3 months.

Refrigerate until ready to use.

metadata.title: Sesame Chicken Noodle Soup
metadata.description: Taiwanese-inspired sesame chicken noodle soup with a ginger-scallion broth rich in sesame oil and rendered chicken fat. Cozy and healing in 20 minutes.
metadata.nutrition-note: Macros vary by noodle type and vegetable choice.
metadata.long_description: A quicker, alcohol-free take on Taiwanese Sesame Oil Chicken Soup (麻油雞). The broth is light but rich with sesame oil, ginger, scallion, and rendered chicken fat. Perfect for busy weeknights when you want something cozy and healing. Based on a recipe from Tiffy Cooks.
metadata.longDescription: A quicker, alcohol-free take on Taiwanese Sesame Oil Chicken Soup (麻油雞). The broth is light but rich with sesame oil, ginger, scallion, and rendered chicken fat. Perfect for busy weeknights when you want something cozy and healing. Based on a recipe from Tiffy Cooks.

sections.title: Season the Chicken
steps: Pat 2 boneless chicken thighs(skin-on) dry. Season with 1 teaspoon soy sauce, ½ teaspoon salt, ¼ teaspoon black pepper, and ¼ teaspoon white pepper.

sections.title: Pan-Fry
steps: Heat 2 tablespoons toasted sesame oil in a pot over medium-high heat. Place chicken skin side down and pan-fry for 3 minutes fry per side until golden brown. Remove and set aside.

sections.title: Build the Broth
steps: In the same pot, add 2 pieces sliced fresh ginger(1 inch each) and the white parts of 2 green onions(white and green separated). Sauté for 2-3 minutes until fragrant.
Pour in 3 cups chicken stock and bring to a gentle simmer for 2 minutes.

sections.title: Simmer
steps: Add 2 servings noodles(ramen, udon, or rice noodles) and 1 cup vegetables(bok choy, spinach, mushrooms, or carrots) to the pot. Add the chicken thighs back in.
Simmer for 5-6 minutes simmer until noodles are cooked through and chicken is fully cooked.

sections.title: Serve
steps: Slice the chicken. Ladle into bowls and garnish with the green parts of the green onions. Serve hot.

sourceText:
== Season the Chicken ==

Pat @boneless chicken thighs{2}(skin-on) dry. Season with @soy sauce{1%teaspoon}, @salt{½%teaspoon}, @black pepper{¼%teaspoon}, and @white pepper{¼%teaspoon}.

== Pan-Fry ==

Heat @toasted sesame oil{2%tablespoons} in a #pot{} over medium-high heat. Place chicken skin side down and pan-fry for ~fry{3%minutes} per side until golden brown. Remove and set aside.

== Build the Broth ==

In the same pot, add @sliced fresh ginger{2%pieces}(1 inch each) and the white parts of @green onions{2}(white and green separated). Sauté for ~{2-3%minutes} until fragrant.

Pour in @chicken stock{3%cups} and bring to a gentle simmer for ~{2%minutes}.

== Simmer ==

Add @noodles{2%servings}(ramen, udon, or rice noodles) and @vegetables{1%cup}(bok choy, spinach, mushrooms, or carrots) to the pot. Add the chicken thighs back in.

Simmer for ~simmer{5-6%minutes} until noodles are cooked through and chicken is fully cooked.

== Serve ==

Slice the chicken. Ladle into bowls and garnish with the green parts of the green onions. Serve hot.

metadata.title: Sheet Pan Chicken and Sweet Potato Meal Prep
metadata.description: Sheet Pan Chicken and Sweet Potato Meal Prep
metadata.author: Lindsay
metadata.longDescription: Great for weekly meal prep, divide into containers for ready-to-go meal starters.

sections.title: Marinate Chicken
steps: Preheat the oven to @425 degrees{}.

Toss 2 lbs boneless skinless chicken breasts(cut into small pieces) with 3 tablespoons spicy seasoning mix and a quick stream of 3 tablespoons olive oil. Stir to combine and store in the fridge for about 30 minutes marinate while you prep other ingredients.

sections.title: Prep Sheet Pans
steps: Arrange 3 sweet potatoes(peeled and diced) on a sheet pan, preferably one with edges to catch drips.
Arrange 5 cups broccoli florets on a separate sheet pan.
Drizzle vegetables with olive oil and sprinkle generously with coarse sea salt and freshly cracked pepper.
Arrange the chicken on a separate sheet pan.

sections.title: Bake
steps: Bake all ingredients for 12-15 minutes first bake. Remove the broccoli and chicken. Stir sweet potatoes and roast for 15 minutes second bake or so.

sections.title: Serve
steps: Divide servings into containers. Serve with avocado / hummus / lemon juice / chives / olive oil.

Toss @boneless skinless chicken breasts{2%lbs}(cut into small pieces) with @spicy seasoning mix{3%tablespoons} and a quick stream of @olive oil{3%tablespoons}. Stir to combine and store in the fridge for about ~marinate{30%minutes} while you prep other ingredients.

metadata.title: Sheet Pan Garlic Ginger Chicken and Broccoli
metadata.description: Sheet Pan Garlic Ginger Chicken and Broccoli
metadata.author: Lindsay
metadata.long_description: Sheet pan chicken and broccoli with a sweet garlic-ginger date sauce, finished with a drizzle of thickened sauce and sesame toppings.
metadata.longDescription: Sheet pan chicken and broccoli with a sweet garlic-ginger date sauce, finished with a drizzle of thickened sauce and sesame toppings.

sections.title: Garlic Ginger Sauce
steps: Blend 3/4 cup low sodium soy sauce, 1/2 cup water, 1/4 cup white vinegar, 1/4 cup olive oil, 1 piece fresh ginger(peeled, 2-inch knob), 4 cloves garlic, and 4 medjool dates in a blender until smooth.
> You can substitute 1/4 cup honey or sugar for the medjool dates.

sections.title: Sheet Pan Action
steps: Preheat the oven to @425 degrees{}.
Place 1 lb boneless skinless chicken breasts(cut into strips), 1 head broccoli(cut into florets), and 1 red pepper(cut into strips) on a sheet pan.
Pour about 1/2 cup sauce over the chicken and a few tablespoons over the veggies. Bake for 12-15 minutes roast.

sections.title: Finish It Fancy
steps: While the broccoli and chicken are roasting, simmer another 1/2 cup or so of sauce in a small saucepan over medium low heat until thickened.
Drizzle the thickened sauce over the finished chicken and broccoli. Finish with sesame oil, sesame seeds, and green onions.

metadata.title: Shepherd's Pie
metadata.description: Classic Shepherd's Pie with ground beef (or lamb) and vegetables in a rich gravy, topped with cheesy mashed potatoes.

sections.title: Meat Filling
steps: Add 2 tbsp olive oil to a large skillet and place over medium-high heat for 2 minutes. Add 1 cup yellow onion, chopped. Cook 5 minutes, stirring occasionally.

Add 1 lb ground beef (or ground lamb) to the skillet and break it apart. Add 2 tsp dried parsley, 1 tsp dried rosemary, 1 tsp dried thyme, 0.5 tsp salt, and 0.5 tsp black pepper. Stir well. Cook for 6-8 minutes until the meat is browned, stirring occasionally.
Add 1 tbsp Worcestershire sauce and 2 cloves garlic, minced. Stir to combine. Cook for 1 minute.
Add 2 tbsp all purpose flour and 2 tbsp tomato paste. Stir until well incorporated and no clumps of tomato paste remain.
Add 1 cup beef broth, 1 cup frozen peas and carrots, and 0.5 cup frozen corn. Bring the liquid to a boil then reduce to simmer. Simmer for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Set the meat mixture aside. Preheat oven to 400 degrees F.

sections.title: Potato Topping
steps: Place 1.75 lb russet potatoes (about 2 large potatoes, peeled and cut into 1 inch cubes) in a large pot. Cover with water. Bring to a boil. Reduce to a simmer. Cook until potatoes are fork tender, 10-15 minutes.
Drain the potatoes in a colander. Return to the hot pot and let rest for 1 minute to evaporate any remaining liquid.
Add 8 tbsp unsalted butter (1 stick), 0.3 cup half and half, 0.5 tsp garlic powder, 0.5 tsp salt, and 0.25 tsp black pepper. Mash the potatoes and stir until all ingredients are mixed together.
Add 0.25 cup parmesan cheese and stir until well combined.

sections.title: Assemble and Bake
steps: Pour the meat mixture into a 9x9 (or 7x11) inch baking dish. Spread into an even layer. Spoon the mashed potatoes on top of the meat. Carefully spread into an even layer.
> If the baking dish looks very full, place it on a rimmed baking sheet so that the filling doesn't bubble over into your oven.
Bake uncovered for 25-30 minutes. Cool for 15 minutes before serving.
> If you can't find frozen mixed peas and carrots, use 0.5 cup frozen peas and 0.5 cup frozen sliced carrots.

metadata.title: Shrimp Asparagus Stir Fry
metadata.description: Juicy plump shrimp and crisp tender asparagus in a light soy-sesame sauce. A healthy 15-minute stir-fry that always impresses.
metadata.nutrition-note: A light, low-carb dish. Doesn't include rice.
metadata.long_description: A quick, healthy stir-fry with juicy shrimp and crisp asparagus in a pantry-friendly soy-sesame sauce. Chop, mix, and sauté, done in 15 minutes. Great for lunch boxes or last-minute dinners. Based on a recipe from Tiffy Cooks.
metadata.longDescription: A quick, healthy stir-fry with juicy shrimp and crisp asparagus in a pantry-friendly soy-sesame sauce. Chop, mix, and sauté, done in 15 minutes. Great for lunch boxes or last-minute dinners. Based on a recipe from Tiffy Cooks.

sections.title: Make the Sauce
steps: In a small bowl, whisk together ¼ cup vegetable stock, 1 teaspoon cornstarch, 1 teaspoon soy sauce, ½ teaspoon toasted sesame oil, ⅛ teaspoon white pepper, and ¼ teaspoon sugar. Set aside.

sections.title: Cook the Shrimp
steps: Heat 1 tablespoon neutral oil in a wok or large pan over medium-high heat. Add 1 lb shrimp(peeled and deveined) and sauté for 3-4 minutes until pink. Transfer to a plate.

sections.title: Cook the Asparagus
steps: In the same pan, add 1 bundle asparagus(trimmed and cut into 2-inch pieces) and sauté for 2-3 minutes until crisp-tender.

sections.title: Combine
steps: Return the shrimp to the pan. Give the sauce a stir to recombine and pour it in, tossing everything together. Cook for 1-2 minutes, stirring constantly, until the sauce thickens and coats the shrimp and asparagus.
Serve immediately.

sourceText:
== Make the Sauce ==

In a #small bowl{}, whisk together @vegetable stock{¼%cup}, @cornstarch{1%teaspoon}, @soy sauce{1%teaspoon}, @toasted sesame oil{½%teaspoon}, @white pepper{⅛%teaspoon}, and @sugar{¼%teaspoon}. Set aside.

== Cook the Shrimp ==

Heat @neutral oil{1%tablespoon} in a #wok{} or #large pan{} over medium-high heat. Add @shrimp{1%lb}(peeled and deveined) and sauté for ~{3-4%minutes} until pink. Transfer to a plate.

== Cook the Asparagus ==

In the same pan, add @asparagus{1%bundle}(trimmed and cut into 2-inch pieces) and sauté for ~{2-3%minutes} until crisp-tender.

== Combine ==

Return the shrimp to the pan. Give the sauce a stir to recombine and pour it in, tossing everything together. Cook for ~{1-2%minutes}, stirring constantly, until the sauce thickens and coats the shrimp and asparagus.

Serve immediately.

metadata.title: Shu Mai
metadata.description: Steamed Chinese open-faced dumplings with pork, shrimp, and shiitake, from a Chinese chef's family recipe.
metadata.nutrition-note: Estimate for full batch of 20 dumplings

sections.title: Prep
steps: Mince 8 oz pork shoulder butt into small bits. Soak in water and massage for 1–2 minutes, then let sit for 10 minutes. Drain in a colander and squeeze out as much water as possible.
Wrap 4 oz shrimp(peeled and deveined) in a paper towel and squeeze out moisture. Mince into fine bits.
Reconstitute 4 pieces dried shiitake mushrooms in hot water for 10 minutes. Squeeze out water, slice in half lengthwise, then mince into fine bits.
Mince 0.5 oz carrot into very fine bits for garnish. Set aside.

sections.title: Marinade
steps: In a bowl, mix 1 tbsp light soy sauce, 2 tbsp oyster sauce, 0.5 tsp salt, 2 tsp sugar, 2 tbsp cornstarch, 0.5 tsp baking soda, 1 tsp chicken bouillon, 2 tbsp water, and 0.5 tsp white pepper.

sections.title: Marinate
steps: Add the pork to the marinade and mix for 2 minutes to help tenderize. Let the pork absorb the sauce for 10 minutes.
Add the minced shrimp and mushrooms, along with 1 tsp olive oil and 1 tbsp sesame oil. Mix for another 1 minute. Cover and refrigerate for 4–8 hours.

sections.title: Fold
steps: Lay a 20 pieces siu mai wrapper in your non-dominant palm. Scoop about 1 oz of filling onto the wrapper and loosely flatten.

Make a circle with your index finger and thumb. Place the wrapper over the hole and use the opposite end of a spoon to push into the center. Compress the meat by pressing with the spoon and squeezing with your fingers on all sides. Rotate and repeat.
Squeeze the bottom half to force meat to rise, then flatten the top with the spoon.
> To freeze: lay siu mai on a tray without touching, freeze for 1–2 hours, then transfer to an airtight bag. Do not steam before freezing. Thaw completely before steaming.

sections.title: Steam
steps: Fill a steamer with about 2 cups water. Arrange siu mai on a steamer rack so they're not touching. Bring water to a boil, set the rack in the steamer, cover, and steam for 10 minutes (or 12 minutes if using a wok-and-plate setup).
Garnish with the minced carrots and serve immediately.

metadata.title: Sichuan Chili Oil
metadata.description: Aromatic Sichuan chili oil infused with peppercorns, star anise, and dried chilies, a versatile condiment for noodles, dumplings, and stir-fries.

sections.title: Prepare the Chili Mixture
steps: Add 8 ounces ground dried chilies(roughly ground, at least half a pound; any kind and heat level) to a large heatproof mixing bowl. Add 0.5 cup Sichuan peppercorns(fresh as possible), 1 tablespoon salt, and 2 tablespoon soy sauce. Stir to combine and set aside.

sections.title: Infuse the Oil
steps: Pour 1.5 quarts canola oil into a heavy-bottomed saucepan. Add 1 head garlic(whole, separated into cloves and lightly smashed), 1 piece ginger(a 3-inch nub, sliced), 3 pieces star anise, 2 tablespoons coriander seeds, 2 pieces cinnamon sticks, 2 pods black cardamom, and 2 pods green cardamom.
Heat over low heat. Keep the garlic and ginger at a gentle fizz, do not let them brown or burn. Simmer for 2 hours infusing until the oil is deeply fragrant.
> This is the most important step. Low and slow infusion builds deep, complex flavor. Watch carefully to ensure nothing browns.

sections.title: Combine Oil and Chilies
steps: When the infused oil is ready, turn the heat up to high. When the ginger and garlic are furiously fizzing, carefully pour the hot oil through a fine-mesh sieve into the chili mixture in the heatproof mixing bowl.
> Be very careful, the oil will be extremely hot and will foam up when it hits the chilies. Chefs in Sichuan say that foaming is a good sign!

sections.title: Cool and Store
steps: Let the chili oil cool to room temperature, about 2 hours cooling.
Once cooled, pour into glass jars, large jars for personal use, smaller jars if giving as gifts.
> The chili oil will taste even better after a few days as the flavors meld. It keeps practically indefinitely, especially stored in the fridge.

metadata.title: Sichuan-Style Fish-Fragrant Eggplant
metadata.description: Stir-fried eggplant with chiles, garlic, ginger, vinegar, and optional minced pork in a fish-fragrant sauce.
metadata.long_description: Eggplant needs to be brined before stir-frying to break down its structure and prevent it from absorbing excess moisture. Shallow-frying in the wok produces great browning with less oil than deep-frying.
metadata.longDescription: Eggplant needs to be brined before stir-frying to break down its structure and prevent it from absorbing excess moisture. Shallow-frying in the wok produces great browning with less oil than deep-frying.

sections.title: Brine the Eggplant
steps: Combine 0.5 cup kosher salt with 2 quarts water in a medium bowl. Add 1 pound Chinese eggplant, cut for stir-fries. Cover with a clean paper towel, press down to soak the paper towel in brine, and set aside to soak 10 minutes to 20 minutes.

Drain the eggplant and spin in a salad spinner or blot dry with paper towels or a clean kitchen towel. Transfer to a bowl, sprinkle with 2 tsp cornstarch, and toss with your fingertips until lightly coated. Set aside.

sections.title: Make the Sauce
steps: Combine 2 tsp Chinkiang vinegar, 2 tsp pickling liquid from pickled chiles, 2 tsp light soy sauce, 1 tsp dark soy sauce, 1 tbsp sugar, 2 tbsp chicken stock, a pinch of kosher salt, and a pinch of MSG (optional), along with 1 tsp cornstarch in a small bowl and mix with a fork until no lumps remain. Set aside.
> If you prefer a milder version, omit the pickled chiles and use distilled white vinegar in place of the pickling liquid.

sections.title: Before You Stir-Fry, Get Your Bowls Ready
steps: a. Brined eggplant
b. Ground pork (if using)
c. Garlic, ginger, chile broad bean paste, scallions, and pickled chiles (if using)
d. Sauce
e. Empty bowl for cooked ingredients
f. Serving platter

sections.title: Stir-Fry
steps: Heat a wok over high heat until lightly smoking. Add 0.25 cup peanut oil and swirl to coat. Reduce the heat to medium-high. Add the eggplant and spread into a single layer. Cook, turning the eggplant occasionally, until softened and well browned on all sides, about 4 minutes. Transfer the eggplant to an empty bowl and set aside.

Return the wok to high heat until lightly smoking. Add the remaining 2 tbsp peanut oil and swirl to coat. Add 2 tbsp garlic minced, 2 tsp fresh ginger minced, 1 tbsp Sichuan chile broad bean paste, 2 scallions scallion whites and pale greens cut into 1-inch segments, and 1 tsp pickled chiles minced (optional) and stir-fry until fragrant and the oil has become dark red from the bean paste, about 30 seconds.
Stir the sauce and add it to the wok by swirling it around the sides. Stir-fry until the sauce is thickened and glossy, about 15 seconds.

sections.title: Finish and Serve
steps: Return the eggplant to the wok and toss to coat in the sauce. If the sauce overthickens and becomes gloppy, thin it out with a splash of water.
Transfer to a serving bowl, garnish with 2 scallions scallion dark greens thinly sliced and fresh cilantro chopped (optional), and serve.
> The ground pork is optional. Omit it to make the dish entirely vegan.

metadata.title: Simple Daikon Radish Soup

sections.title: Prepare the Vegetables
steps: Slice the 300 gram daikon radish into small pieces.
Slice the 1 long onion into small pieces.

sections.title: Cook the Daikon
steps: In a large pot, combine the 1200 ml kombu dashi, 1 clove garlic grated, and daikon slices.

> For a vegan-friendly version, make sure to use a kombu-based dashi powder or make your own kombu dashi from scratch. The simplicity of this recipe allows the natural flavor of the daikon to shine through, making it a perfect light meal or starter.

metadata.title: Siopao
metadata.description: Filipino steamed pork buns with soft, fluffy bread and a sweet-savory asado filling.
metadata.author: Lalaine Manalo
metadata.nutrition-note: Estimate for full batch of 10 buns including filling, dough, and sauce

sections.title: Asado Filling
steps: In a pot over medium heat, heat 1 tbsp canola oil. Add 1 onion(chopped) and 2 cloves garlic(minced), cook until softened.
Add 1 lb pork butt(cut into large chunks) and cook, turning, until lightly browned.

Add 2 cups water, 0.33 cup soy sauce, 2 tbsp oyster sauce, 3 tbsp sugar, and 2 pieces star anise. Stir and bring to a boil, skimming scum. Lower heat, cover, and cook for 1 hour until meat is fork-tender. Add water in half-cup increments as needed to maintain about 1.5 cups liquid.
With a slotted spoon, remove pork and let cool. Shred with two forks. Reserve about 1 cup of braising liquid and set aside. Return shredded meat to pot and bring to a boil.

Combine 1 tbsp cornstarch and about 0.25 cup water in a small bowl, stirring until smooth. Add half the slurry to the pot of meat and cook for 2 minutes until thickened. Remove from heat and cool completely.

In a saucepan over medium heat, combine the reserved braising liquid with the remaining cornstarch slurry. Bring to a boil, stirring, for 2 minutes until thickened. This is the siopao sauce. Set aside.
> Cool the filling completely before using, escaping steam can tear the dough. Filling can be made ahead and refrigerated up to 3 days.

sections.title: Dough
steps: In a bowl, combine 260 ml warm milk(105–115°F), 2 tsp dry instant yeast, 2 tbsp sugar, and 0.5 tsp salt. Stir until dissolved and let stand for 5 minutes until foamy.
In a large bowl, combine 500 g all-purpose flour, 100 g sugar, 2 tsp baking powder, and 2 tbsp vegetable oil. Mix well. Add a few drops of lime juice.
Add the yeast mixture to the flour mixture. Mix and knead until the dough is smooth and no longer sticky.
Cover with a kitchen towel and let rise in a warm place for 2 hours until doubled.
Turn dough out onto a clean surface and form into a long log. Cut into 10 equal pieces and roll each into a ball. Cover and let rise for 30 minutes.

sections.title: Assembly
steps: Roll each dough ball into a 4–5 inch round, keeping edges thinner than the center. Place about 1 tablespoon of filling in the center.
Gather the edges, pleat around the filling, and twist to seal. Place on a piece of parchment paper. Repeat with remaining dough and filling.
Arrange buns on a baking sheet, cover with a towel, and let rise for 10 minutes.

sections.title: Steam
steps: In a steamer, arrange buns in a single layer, 1 inch apart. Add 2 tbsp vinegar to the steaming water for whiter buns.
Steam on low heat for 15 minutes. Keep the lid on for 5 minutes after turning off heat to prevent deflating.
> Cover the steamer lid with a towel to keep condensation from dripping on the buns.
Serve with the asado sauce.

metadata.title: Soft Sourdough Rolls
metadata.description: Light, moist, and buttery sourdough rolls with a distinct tangy flavor and pleasing chew from ripe sourdough starter. Baked clustered together in round pans for soft, pillowy texture.

sections.title: Dough
steps: Weigh your flour or measure it by gently spooning it into a cup, then sweeping off any excess. Combine 113 gram sourdough starter (ripe/fed), 227 gram water (lukewarm), 300 gram all-purpose flour, 9 gram salt, 2 tbsp granulated sugar, 85 gram unsalted butter (room temperature), 28 gram dry milk, 46 gram potato flour, and 1.5 tsp instant yeast. Mix and knead by hand, mixer, or bread machine set on the dough cycle, adding more flour or water if necessary to make a soft, smooth dough.
Place the dough into a lightly greased bowl, cover, and allow it to rise at warm room temperature until nearly doubled in bulk, 60 minutes to 90 minutes.

sections.title: Shape
steps: While the dough is rising, lightly grease two 8" round cake pans.
Transfer the dough to a lightly greased work surface, gently deflate it, and divide it into 16 pieces.
Shape each piece of dough into a ball. Place eight balls in each of the round pans, spacing them evenly so they do not touch one another.
Cover the pans and allow the rolls to rise until they touch one another and are very puffy, 60 minutes to 90 minutes.

sections.title: Bake
steps: While the rolls are rising, preheat the oven to 350F.
Bake the sourdough rolls for 24 minutes to 26 minutes, until they are a light golden brown on top. A digital thermometer inserted into one of the center rolls should read 190F.
Remove the sourdough rolls from the oven and after 3 minutes, carefully transfer them to a cooling rack to cool.
> Store leftover rolls well-wrapped at room temperature for several days. Freeze wrapped airtight for up to three months.
> If you do not have sourdough starter, you will need to make a homemade starter and feed it for 5 to 7 days before it is ready for baking.

metadata.title: Sourdough Bagels
metadata.description: Freshly made bagels with a crispy outside and chewy inside. These require some exotic ingredients like diastatic malt and barley syrup.

steps: Levain (the night before mixing, 9:30 p.m.): Mix all the Levain ingredients in a container and leave it at a warm temperature for 12 hours.

Mix (9:30 a.m.): Add a splash of the mixing water, 29 g sugar, 29 g barley malt syrup, 7 g diastatic malt powder, and 18 g salt to a small bowl and mix together. To your stand mixer's mixing bowl, add the malt syrup slurry, 848 g bread flour, 472 g water, and 200 g ripe levain.
Mix on low speed for approximately 5 minutes until the dough strengthens and begins to smooth. Add stand mixer lid to stand mixer bowl.
Bulk Fermentation (9:45 a.m. to 12:45 p.m.): Give this dough a single fold after 1.5 hours into bulk fermentation.
Divide and Shape (12:45 p.m.): Use a baking sheet (so it fits into your refrigerator) to hold the 12 pieces of shaped dough. Spread a thin layer of cornmeal on the half sheet to prevent sticking.

Divide the dough into twelve 125g pieces. First, degas the piece by tamping down a bit with your hand. Then, form the piece into a rough rectangle and cinch down from the top, so the dough ends up in a little tube. Roll the tube out to a 12-inch long tube. Wrap the dough around the backside of your hand and pinch it together in the front. Roll a few times on the counter to seal. Transfer to the cornmeal-dusted baking sheet. Repeat for remaining dough pieces.

Proof (1:00 p.m. to 3:00 p.m.): Cover the baking sheet with a large reusable plastic bag and seal shut. Let the dough proof at room temperature, around 72-74°F (22-23°C), for 2 hours. The dough should puff up slightly after this time but not excessively. If the dough still feels very dense to the touch, give it another 15-30 minutes and check again. After 2 hours, place the covered baking sheet into the fridge overnight at around 39°F (4°C).
Boil and Top (9:30 a.m., Day Three): Oven prep: Before you begin boiling your bagel dough, preheat your oven to 475°F (245°C) with convection or 500°F (260°C) without convection.

Boiling equipment prep: Fill a wide pot with water and bring to a low boil. Next to your stovetop, place a half baking sheet with a cooling rack inside, this will hold the wet bagels for a minute and allow them to drain. Next, line a full baking sheet with parchment paper,this will hold the dough as it bakes. Finally, grab any toppings you'd like (poppy, oat, everything bagel mix, sesame, etc.) and place them in bowls on your work surface.

Boil: Once the water is at a low boil, boil the proofed sourdough bagel dough straight from the fridge, about 40 seconds per side. Using a spider strainer, transfer each piece to the cooling rack inside the baking sheet to drain while you boil the rest of the dough. Then, transfer the boiled bagels to the full baking sheet and top, if desired.
Bake (9:45 a.m.): Slide the pan with all the bagel dough into the oven and add an ice cube to the tray. Quickly close the oven.
Bake at 475°F (245°C) convection (500°F (260°C) without convection) for 10 minutes.
After 10 minutes, rotate the baking sheet 180°, and bake for 5 minutes longer.
After this 5 minutes, turn the oven down to 450°F (235°C) and bake for 5 minutes longer for a total of 20 minutes.
Remove the sheet when the bagels are nicely colored. Let cool 15-20 minutes on a wire rack.

sourceText:
Levain (the night before mixing, 9:30 p.m.): Mix all the Levain ingredients in a container and leave it at a warm temperature for ~{12%hours}.

Mix (9:30 a.m.): Add a splash of the mixing water, @sugar{29%g}, @barley malt syrup{29%g}, @diastatic malt powder{7%g}, and @salt{18%g} to a #small bowl{} and mix together. To your #stand mixer{}'s mixing bowl, add the malt syrup slurry, @bread flour{848%g}, @water{472%g}, and @ripe levain{200%g}.

Mix on low speed for approximately ~{5%minutes} until the dough strengthens and begins to smooth. Add #stand mixer lid{} to #stand mixer bowl{}.

Bulk Fermentation (9:45 a.m. to 12:45 p.m.): Give this dough a single fold after ~{1.5%hours} into bulk fermentation.

Divide and Shape (12:45 p.m.): Use a #baking sheet{} (so it fits into your refrigerator) to hold the 12 pieces of shaped dough. Spread a thin layer of @cornmeal{} on the #half sheet{} to prevent sticking.

Divide the dough into twelve 125g pieces. First, degas the piece by tamping down a bit with your hand. Then, form the piece into a rough rectangle and cinch down from the top, so the dough ends up in a little tube. Roll the tube out to a 12-inch long tube. Wrap the dough around the backside of your hand and pinch it together in the front. Roll a few times on the counter to seal. Transfer to the cornmeal-dusted baking sheet. Repeat for remaining dough pieces.

Proof (1:00 p.m. to 3:00 p.m.): Cover the baking sheet with a #large reusable plastic bag{} and seal shut. Let the dough proof at room temperature, around 72-74°F (22-23°C), for ~{2%hours}. The dough should puff up slightly after this time but not excessively. If the dough still feels very dense to the touch, give it another 15-30 minutes and check again. After 2 hours, place the covered baking sheet into the fridge overnight at around 39°F (4°C).

Boil and Top (9:30 a.m., Day Three): Oven prep: Before you begin boiling your bagel dough, preheat your oven to 475°F (245°C) with convection or 500°F (260°C) without convection.

Boiling equipment prep: Fill a #wide pot{} with water and bring to a low boil. Next to your stovetop, place a half baking sheet with a cooling rack inside, this will hold the wet bagels for a minute and allow them to drain. Next, line a full baking sheet with parchment paper,this will hold the dough as it bakes. Finally, grab any toppings you'd like (poppy, oat, everything bagel mix, sesame, etc.) and place them in bowls on your work surface.

Boil: Once the water is at a low boil, boil the proofed sourdough bagel dough straight from the fridge, about ~{40%seconds} per side. Using a spider #strainer{}, transfer each piece to the cooling rack inside the baking sheet to drain while you boil the rest of the dough. Then, transfer the boiled bagels to the full baking sheet and top, if desired.

Bake (9:45 a.m.): Slide the pan with all the bagel dough into the oven and add an ice cube to the tray. Quickly close the oven.

Bake at 475°F (245°C) convection (500°F (260°C) without convection) for ~{10%minutes}.

After 10 minutes, rotate the baking sheet 180°, and bake for ~{5%minutes} longer.

After this 5 minutes, turn the oven down to 450°F (235°C) and bake for ~{5%minutes} longer for a total of 20 minutes.

Remove the sheet when the bagels are nicely colored. Let cool 15-20 minutes on a wire rack.

metadata.title: Sourdough Banana Bread
metadata.description: Banana bread with sourdough discard for a subtle tang that balances the sweetness of bananas and honey.

steps: Preheat the oven to 325F. Lightly grease a 9" x 5" loaf pan.

In a large mixing bowl, combine the 113 gram unsalted butter, 142 gram light brown sugar, 1 tsp vanilla extract, 1 tsp cinnamon, 1/4 tsp nutmeg, 1 tsp baking soda, 1 tsp baking powder, and 1 tsp table salt, beating until smooth.
Add the 397 gram mashed ripe banana, 85 gram honey, 2 eggs, and 113 gram sourdough starter discard, again beating until smooth.
Add the 240 gram all-purpose flour then the 85 gram chopped nuts, stirring just until smooth.
Transfer the batter to the prepared loaf pan, smoothing the top. Let it rest at room temperature for 10 minutes.
Bake the bread for 45 minutes, then gently lay a piece of aluminum foil across the top to prevent over-browning.

Bake for an additional 25 minutes. A long toothpick or thin paring knife inserted into the center should come out clean, with a few wet crumbs clinging to it. If it shows any sign of uncooked batter, bake an additional 5 minutes.
> Feel free to use fed/ripe starter instead of discard, if desired.
Allow the bread to cool for 10 minutes in the pan. Remove it from the pan and cool completely on a wire rack.
Store leftover bread, tightly wrapped, at room temperature for several days. Freeze for longer storage.
